title: Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks
principal_findings: DNNs rely on unintended shortcuts (e.g. background, texture) that fail under distribution shift.
limitations: Conceptual framework; does not provide spatial MRI protocols.
relevance_to_our_work: Theoretical foundation for shortcut learning terminology and mechanisms.
reviewer_notes: Foundational reference for shortcut learning concept.

title: AI for radiographic COVID-19 detection frequently relies on superficial shortcuts
principal_findings: COVID-19 classifiers heavily exploit hospital-specific markers, arrows, and positioning rather than lung pathology.
limitations: Focuses on chest X-rays and text/border markers; no perilesional margin or distant scrambling.
relevance_to_our_work: Landmark proof that medical classifiers exploit non-pathological shortcuts.
reviewer_notes: Key evidence that high test accuracy does not equal pathology reliance.

title: Variable generalization performance of a deep learning model to detect pneumonia in chest radiographs
principal_findings: Models exploit scanner vendor differences and metal tokens to achieve high within-hospital accuracy but fail externally.
limitations: Observational multi-hospital audit; no targeted in silico surgical spatial interventions.
relevance_to_our_work: Demonstrates that hospital metadata and scanner signatures act as primary confounders.
reviewer_notes: Demonstrates that multi-site generalizability requires controlling confounders.

title: (De)Constructing Bias on Skin Lesion Datasets
principal_findings: Classifiers achieve high diagnostic accuracy even when the entire melanoma lesion is masked out (Skin-Only).
limitations: 2D dermoscopy images; no paired patient-cluster bootstrap; no margin inpainting or matched placebos.
relevance_to_our_work: Closest medical imaging analogue to our Tumor-Removed and Tumor-Only experiments.
reviewer_notes: Proves that models can classify diseases without looking at the lesion itself.

title: Noise or Signal: The Role of Image Backgrounds in Object Recognition
principal_findings: Classifiers rely on backgrounds to achieve high accuracy; swapping backgrounds drops accuracy by up to 88%.
limitations: Natural images; not medical; ignores medical boundary discontinuities.
relevance_to_our_work: Methodological precedent for separating foreground object from background context.
reviewer_notes: Precedent for foreground/background swap and context dependency.

title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
principal_findings: Introduced sliding-window occlusion sensitivity to verify whether CNNs localize primary objects.
limitations: Fixed square gray patch; ignores anatomical borders and perilesional margins.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational origin of occlusion sensitivity testing in neural networks.

title: Interpretable Explanations of Black Boxes by Meaningful Perturbation
principal_findings: Proved that naive zero-filling introduces artificial high-frequency edge artifacts that distort CNN explanations.
limitations: Framed as an optimization problem for attribution heatmaps rather than controlled lesion hypothesis testing.
relevance_to_our_work: Directly justifies our use of smooth Navier-Stokes inpainting over zero-filling.
reviewer_notes: Essential justification for why zero-filling confounds margin ablation.

title: Image Inpainting
principal_findings: Established PDE isophote transport for digital inpainting, eliminating boundary step discontinuities.
limitations: Pure graphics/image restoration paper; not a medical shortcut or classification study.
relevance_to_our_work: Algorithmic source of our Navier-Stokes margin inpainting implementation (cv2.INPAINT_NS).

title: Scores That Hold, Benchmarks That Leak: Measuring Dataset Contamination in Public Brain-Tumor MRI Classification
principal_findings: 95.5% of traceable test slices share patient overlap; file headers alone classify tumors at 0.959 accuracy.
limitations: Focuses on dataset contamination and leakage auditing; does not conduct spatial surgical lesion interventions.
relevance_to_our_work: Directly audits our exact benchmark dataset and establishes the necessity of patient-level splits.
reviewer_notes: Audits the exact Cheng dataset and validates our split strategy.

title: Enhanced Performance of Brain Tumor Classification via Tumor Region Augmentation and Partition
principal_findings: Original dataset creator paper; demonstrated that dilating tumor margins into ring-form partitions improves classification.
limitations: Classical SVM / Bag-of-Words features; no deep learning; random slice-level splits (unaware of patient leakage).
relevance_to_our_work: Original source of the 15-pixel dilation margin concept and the Figshare dataset itself.
reviewer_notes: Source of the dataset and concentric ring dilation concept.

title: TACE: Tumor-Aware Counterfactual Explanations
principal_findings: Uses generative inpainting constrained strictly to tumor ROIs to generate plausible counterfactuals.
limitations: Evaluates generative latent diffusion; lacks matched placebos, margin sweeps, or patient-cluster bootstrap.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent direct prior art applying inpainting specifically to brain MRI tumor regions.
reviewer_notes: Directly connects tumor ROI inpainting with counterfactual explanation.

title: Causality matters in medical imaging
principal_findings: Frames medical imaging tasks under causal DAGs; proves that in silico interventions probe model anti-causal associations, not pathology.
limitations: Theoretical perspective; no empirical MRI tumor intervention experiments.
relevance_to_our_work: Crucial methodological justification for why our study cannot claim biological or cellular causality.
reviewer_notes: Provides the causal inference boundary for our claims.
